correctness.rationale: With standard normalized Szego kernels, the exact Berezin transform is z(a+b|z|^2)/(1+|z|^2). The shift norm is max(|a|,|b|), and half-line Jacobi row-sum and long-block estimates give numerical radius (|a|+|b|)/2. For |a|>=|b| evaluation at radius 1/2 gives a strict ratio > both proposed constants. For |b|>=|a|, evaluations at radii sqrt(2)-1 and approaching 1 give two monotone lower envelopes meeting uniquely at |a/b|=4sqrt(2)-5. Equality forces anti-phase. Exact derivative signs prove that this profile actually has Berezin number (3-2sqrt(2))|b|, attained at radius sqrt(2)-1. The quadratic-field identities were checked by the packaged script; finite tests are auxiliary, not proof.

value.rationale: Normalized-kernel testing is a natural practical surrogate for the full numerical radius and operator norm. The first nontrivial periodic shift family has a nontrivial cancellation mechanism: both natural sharp lower ratios admit exact, different constants but share a unique complex anti-phase extremizer. This produces a quantitative, attained benchmark for how much infinite-dimensional Berezin testing can miss, not merely a renamed textbook identity or an arbitrary finite slice.
